version.changelog: InkOS v1.8.0: unified pi-agent production harness, professional Skills, BM25 retrieval, book-bound references, atomic chapter workspaces, and TUI confirmation/model controls.

llm.summary: InkOS is coherent for story creation, but it should be reviewed before install because it pulls an unpinned external npm CLI that may handle your API key and writing files.

dimensions.detail: Model-provider setup, custom provider URLs, search credentials, local skill directories, and external LLM/image/search calls are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users must treat provider endpoints and API-key exposure carefully.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install metadata references the executable npm package @actalk/inkos without an exact version, lockfile, or integrity hash in the submitted artifact, while the package will operate with user permissions and the declared OPENAI_API_KEY environment.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions emphasize typed actions, explicit user intent, confirmation gates, checking real tool/file results, research only on explicit request, and never auto-executing bundled skill scripts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Project-local JSON state, markdown projections, SQLite memory, optional global config, a localhost Studio service, and daemon mode are disclosed; the artifact says daemon mode is explicit and memory is project/book isolated.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The descriptor consistently describes a broad story, translation, research, image, Studio, CLI, and TUI production system; those capabilities are disclosed and mostly fit the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable running the @actalk/inkos npm CLI with access to your manuscript project and configured API keys. Prefer a pinned, audited package version, use environment or Studio secret storage rather than literal keys, avoid untrusted custom base URLs, and review local persistence, daemon, and localhost Studio settings before using it on sensitive work.
llm.findings:
[AE1] unexpected: Downgraded: the submitted artifact/SKILL.md was locally available and fully read; the scanner's partial-reference concern appears tied to unresolved path-like references rather than hidden executable content in this package.
[EA5] expected: Provider and model configuration is expected for an AI writing tool and is documented as setup; the custom-provider mode is risky because it forwards keys to the chosen endpoint, but the descriptor warns to use only trusted URLs.
[RA2] expected: Story-state persistence is central to long-form writing continuity and is disclosed as project/book-local JSON plus SQLite memory, with inspection and deletion described.
[E1] expected: Sending content to configured LLM endpoints is expected for this tool and disclosed; this is not evidence of hidden exfiltration, but users should review provider data policies.
[EA2] expected: The cited auto-execute text is actually a negative instruction not to auto-execute scripts, and the delete --force option is a documented user-invoked CLI flag rather than an automatic agent action.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese examples match the advertised bilingual writing use case and do not create a security concern.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted as a material Review concern: the npm install target is unpinned and not bundled for audit, so later package changes could affect installed behavior after this descriptor review.
